Changelog ​

User-visible changes in each production release of the Primitive platform: new capabilities, additions and changes to the client APIs and the CLI, and fixes that change behavior you can observe. Internal work — refactoring, infrastructure, dependency bumps — is not listed. Entries are newest first; each date is a production release, grouped by feature area, with Breaking, Deprecated and Fixed tags where they apply. An ## Unreleased section, when present, lists changes already merged since the last production release; it is date-stamped when that release ships.

Unreleased ​

Databases ​

  • A database (db3) is where an app's data lives: created, typed, shared and read through client.db3 in the JavaScript and Swift clients, primitive db3 on the CLI and ctx.db3 in a server function. Each database is synced to its readers' devices, or has sync off and is served only by functions.
  • A database's models are declared once in a db3-types/<type>.toml file: config push generates typed models for the web, iOS and functions (the Db3 namespace of functions/primitive.d.ts), installs the type in every database of it and enforces its models, indexes, unique constraints, timestamps, auto-populated fields and CEL triggers on every writer; primitive db3-types list|get|push-status|push --retry follow a push, primitive db3 type attach types an existing database, a type file cannot be pruned while a database is of it (DB3_TYPE_IN_USE), and a type takes no rule set (DB3_TYPE_RULE_SET_UNSUPPORTED).
  • Once a database of a type exists, config push refuses a type change that would make its stored records unreadable — a removed model or field, a changed field type, a removed enum value or a newly required field — with DB3_TYPE_NOT_APPEND_ONLY, and config push --allow-field-removal pushes one anyway once the app sets allowFieldRemoval = true in app.toml.
  • A db3 field is renamed by changing its key and naming its old name in storedAs: records, indexes and builds generated before keep the stored name and nothing is rewritten, the push answer lists each rename in renamedFields, and primitive db3-types get shows each field's former names.
  • A db3 field is retired in three pushes instead: deprecated = true marks it deprecated in generated code, cleared = true leaves it out of every read, filter and generated model while older builds' writes still succeed, and moving its name into the model's removedFields reserves it for good; primitive db3-types get lists a type's deprecated, cleared and removed fields.
  • archived = true in a type's [type] table, or primitive db3-types archive and unarchive, stops new databases of the type with DB3_TYPE_ARCHIVED while the databases already of it keep working, and primitive db3-types list and get show each type's status.
  • create = "admins" in a type's [type] table keeps creating databases of that type to app admins and owners, and untypedDb3Create = "admins" in app.toml does the same for databases with no type; a member's create is refused with DB3_CREATE_ROLE_REQUIRED.
  • Client codegen reads the whole db3-types/ directory (js-bao-codegen-v2 -i, swift-bao-codegen --input, and inputs in bao-codegen.json) and generates each model once; a model several types hold is declared in one file and named from the others with [type] models, and a model needs no id field.
  • Models generated with --known-types-only make the client refuse to create or open a database of a type the app was not generated with (DB3_TYPE_UNKNOWN_TO_CLIENT on open) unless the call passes allowUnknownType: true, and client.db3.stored() and listMine() mark such a database knownType: false; the web template generates this way, and a bao-codegen.json beside its package.json names the types its pnpm codegen generates.
  • A db3 field can take its values from a string enum declared in schemas/ with ref = "<Name>", "<file>.<Name>" or "schemas.<file>.<Name>": config push sends it as type = "string" with the def's enum, config diff and config pull read the expanded type, and js-bao-codegen-v2 and swift-bao-codegen read schemas/ beside db3-types/ to generate the same models, which type such a field by the enum itself — Status and StatusValues from shared-enums.generated.ts on the web, a Swift enum Status from Primitive.generated.swift on iOS — as the function helpers do.
  • A db3 field can hold a JSON object typed by an object def in schemas/, in beta: ref the def, and the record stores it as JSON text that functions type as Db3Json<Schemas.<Name>> and the web and iOS models generated with js-bao-codegen-v2 --schema-defs-import and swift-bao-codegen read and write as the def's value, checking each save against it; a query can only ask whether it holds a value ($exists).
  • enforce_enum = true beside a db3 type field's enum makes every database of the type refuse a write leaving a value outside the set with DB3_VALUE_NOT_IN_ENUM, from a device, the records routes, ctx.db3, the CLI and a bulk load; the JavaScript and Swift clients refuse it on the device before sending, and a push or attach over a database whose records hold an outside value is refused for that database, naming the field, the count and samples.
  • Records are read and written with the generated models on a device, ctx.db3(id, type).model(name) in a function (ctx.db3(id) for an untyped database, { asUser } to act as a member), and client.db3.records(id) or primitive db3 records over HTTP: cursor-paged queries with $all and $size, counts, grouped aggregates, include for related records, upsertOn, conditional writes and ifNotExists, increment counters, string-set $add, $remove and $clear, atomic or per-operation batches of up to 100 operations that may read between their writes, and batchRead for several reads answered from one state of the database, under one set of limits (100 records a page by default and 10,000 at most, 8 MiB a page, 3 include levels); a call naming a database the app does not have, or one since deleted, is refused DB3_NOT_FOUND.
  • A synced database is subscribed with client.db3.subscribe (available once the device's copy answers queries, ready once it has caught up, state and the db3:* events), reads and writes offline — client.db3.create included, which returns as soon as the database exists on the device, online or offline, and commits it to the server in the background — queues writes, refuses on the device a write the user's permission or the type's declarations would refuse and hands back the rest on db3:write-refused (save({ confirm: true }) waits for the database's answer), turns gone with the reason (permission, sync-off, deleted or client-outdated) when the device loses access and returns to live if access is restored while it is open, is closed when its user signs out or another signs in, and is removed with client.db3.evict or a retention policy.
  • A synced database lives on the device in the browser's origin-private file system on the web — set up by the Vue template with nothing to configure, or in another web app with databaseConfig: { type: "opfs" } and the worker, broker and js-bao/sqlite3.wasm it names — in the app's container on iOS, and in Node.js in memory with databaseConfig: { type: "sqljs" } or on disk in a node-sqlite directory with better-sqlite3 installed, and a device that cannot keep one reports FORMAT2_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE.
  • client.db3.commitCreate commits a database the device created offline and client.db3.cancelPendingCreate cancels it on the device, in beta, in the JavaScript and Swift clients.
  • client.db3.create({ localOnly: true }) creates a database that lives on one device only and is never sent to the server: its writes are checked and confirmed on the device, its indexes (member indexes included) are kept there, and only client.db3.delete or logout({ wipeLocal: true }) removes it.
  • Fields declared indexed or unique are indexed in every database of the type, and client.db3.indexes / primitive db3 indexes register and drop per-database indexes, including named unique constraints and member indexes on string-set fields (members: true, CLI --set-elements) that keep $contains, any-of and facets fast on a large database; on ("both", "server" or "device") chooses where each index is built, member indexes included, and each listed index carries its kind and on.
  • A text index (kind: "text", CLI --kind text) over a model's string fields answers a $search filter on the server and on each device holding the database, in the JavaScript and Swift clients, with every record ranked by its _score.
  • A vector field stores an embedding in the JavaScript and Swift clients, and a vector index (kind: "vector", placed on the device) answers $near queries on each device holding the database, exactly or, with index: { mode: "ann" }, from an approximate index whose model one device trains and every other device fetches.
  • Each device builds the indexes placed on it as they are registered or dropped, without a resubscribe: client.db3.indexes.local lists them with their build status and client.db3.indexes.skipped the ones this device builds nothing for, decline and accept choose which ones this device keeps, and the deviceIndexes client option sets the default.
  • maxDrift on a query, count or queryOne refuses an answer from a device's copy too far behind with DB3_DRIFT_EXCEEDED, and the database's state reports that drift.
  • query, count, aggregate and batch writes answer what they cost the server in cost.rowsRead and cost.rowsWritten, and the analytics/db3/queries and analytics/requests reports rank those costs per query shape, endpoint and function.
  • primitive db3 records query, count and aggregate take --explain to show an app admin or the database's owner how the server answers the read — the indexes it used and the rows it scanned — and --index <name> (or none) to force it onto or off an index, and in development the JavaScript client's devMode: { servedIndexes: true } logs which index served each read on the device.
  • A database download cut short by a reload, a closed tab or app, or a dropped connection continues where it stopped at the next subscribe.
  • A database's image blob shows directly: use its URL as an <img> source on the web, and BlobImage in SwiftUI.
  • primitive db3 list --user-id <id> lists every database a user can open, with a VIA column (--via held,shared,app).
  • Anyone who may write a database renames it with client.db3.update(id, { title }) in the JavaScript and Swift clients, primitive db3 update --title or ctx.api.db3.update, in beta, and the connected devices of its direct-grant holders get the new title at once.
  • An app owner or admin marks a database public with client.db3.permissions(id).setPublicAccess("reader") in the JavaScript and Swift clients, primitive db3 public-access set <db3-id> reader|none or, in a server function declaring db3:setPublicAccess, ctx.api.db3.setPublicAccess, in beta, so functions may serve it to callers who are not signed in while the app's signedOutAccess is on; it is not a sharing level, and client.db3.get shows it to those who manage the database's sharing.
  • A public function serves a database whose id the caller names with requirePublicDb3 or requireDb3Level(…, { orPublic: true }) in its authorize, or reads auth.db3(id, type).publicAccess(), and config push warns about a public function that hands an id from its input to ctx.db3 without checking access to it.
  • Access is per database: share with users, groups (a membership in the group, or the app owner or admin role, is required), a link or the whole app (setAppAccess) — a share email links to the app's base URL unless documentUrl names a page — let members ask with requestAccess and owners hear each request and its resolution live (db3:access-request-created / db3:access-request-resolved), check with client.db3.get, auth.db3(id, type).permissions() or validateAccess, list a user's databases with client.db3.listMine (filtered by via; a sync-off database is listed to no one), cancel one email share before the invitee signs up with permissions(id).revokePendingInvitation, and give a user their own database under a key you choose with getOrCreateWithAlias or bind a key to an existing one with client.db3.aliases.set / resolve / delete, held by that user at owner or, from a function, at the reader or read-write its permission names.
  • primitive db3 permissions, group-permissions, link-access, app-access, access-requests and access list and change a database's sharing from the CLI, and show a user's effective access to it.
  • Every database has a custodian, a member or the app: primitive db3 create --custodian app, db3 list --custodian, db3 transfer, db3 owner-row set and the sync switch (db3 sync set), and ctx.api.db3.create, transfer, setOwnerRow, setSync and setAppAccess under the db3:transfer, db3:setOwnerRow, db3:setSync and db3:setAppAccess capabilities; a departing member's databases pass to the app or are deleted, a transfer to the app removes the previous owner's own grant, and a transfer in progress answers 409 TRANSFER_PENDING to another transfer or owner-row change.
  • client.db3.ingests, primitive db3 ingest and, in a server function, ctx.db3(id, type).load(rows) (read back with loadStatus and loadRefused) bulk-load records (--mode refresh replaces a dataset), and primitive db3 export / import (--into, --keep-id) move a database within or between apps.
  • client.db3.records(id).clear(model) in the JavaScript client, client.db3.clearModel in Swift and primitive db3 records clear empty one model of a database in a single change each device applies whole, and drop: true also removes the model from a database with no type; emptying a model is experimental, so production does not serve it.
  • A server function acting about a member it is not lists that member's databases with ctx.api.db3.listHeldByUser({ userId }) and ctx.api.db3.listSharedWithUser({ userId }) — the entries client.db3.listMine returns for via: "held" and "shared", narrowed by tag and type, the held listing including the member's sync-off databases — and binds, finds and removes one's alias with ctx.api.db3.aliases.set, resolve and delete. A filtered page can be short or empty with hasMore: true; follow nextCursor.
  • A [[function.triggers.db3]] entry runs a function once per batch of changes to any database of a type, admitted by allowCallers({ db3: true }).
  • A database's files are client.db3.blobs(id) on both clients and ctx.api.db3.blobs.upload and download in a function.
  • A server function mints a signed upload URL for a database the app holds with ctx.api.db3.blobs.signedUploadUrl, in beta, and a web page, signed out included, uploads one file to it with client.db3.uploadSigned(url, file): the URL accepts one file of its media type and size before it expires, the blob is recorded as uploaded by the app, and primitive spent-tokens get <tokenId> shows when a URL was used.
  • A blob in a public database has a stable URL anyone can load, signed in or not, while the app's signedOutAccess setting is on: client.db3.publicBlobUrl(db3Id, blobId) in the JavaScript client, in beta, and primitive db3 public-access blob-url <db3-id> <blob-id> build it. Its answer may be cached for five minutes and revalidated with the blob's ETag; every other request answers one 404; each request counts against the signed-out per-address limit and hourly signedOutCeiling, and served requests are metered as signedout.blob.
  • A server function shows a database's images to readers who hold no grant on it with ctx.api.db3.blobs.getSignedUrls, in beta: up to 100 expiring URLs in one call, each loaded with no session and served with the blob's content type. Whoever can download the database's blobs can mint them, userId judges a call by that member's access, and a function a signed-out caller started mints for at most an hour. Deleting the blob or the database makes its URLs answer 404, though a browser can keep a copy it already loaded until the URL expires.
  • ctx.api.blobBuckets.getSignedUrls, in beta, mints up to 100 bucket blob URLs in one call, each checked against the bucket's share rule, and lists the ids with no blob in missing.
  • A database record's upsert names are typed by its model's unique fields and constraints (save's upsertOn, upsertByUnique, and the generated Swift UniqueField and UniqueConstraint), and the server refuses any other upsert target.
  • A web model generated by js-bao-codegen-v2 exports <Model>Filter and <Model>Sort, which refuse a field the model does not have, an operand of the wrong kind and an operator the field's kind does not take; augmenting ModelQueryTyping with enforced: true holds the model's query, queryOne, count and aggregate to the same checks and types each aggregate row's group keys and operation results by name.
  • An iOS model generated by swift-bao-codegen carries a typed token per field on fields, and query(where:), queryPaged(where:), queryOne(where:), count(where:) and aggregate(groupBy:operations:) take filters, sorts, group levels and operations built from them, so a field the model does not have, an operand of the wrong type or an operator the field's kind does not take fails to compile, and each aggregate row answers its group values and results by the key requested; the DocumentFilter reads are unchanged.
  • A refusing trigger whose when can't be evaluated refuses the write with TRIGGER_EVALUATION_FAILED, and config push refuses a trigger expression that can never be evaluated.
  • Deprecated: The documents and databases surfaces this release's databases replace — client.documents, client.document(id), client.databases and client.databaseTypeConfigs with their Swift twins, the document open, sync and awareness methods, collections.listCollectionsForDocument, ctx.doc, ctx.db and ctx.api.documents / ctx.api.databases, and primitive documents, primitive databases and primitive database-type-configs — stay served; each of those CLI commands, and creating a format-1 document, prints a deprecation warning, and new data belongs in a db3.

Agents ​

  • An agent is a prompt of kind = "agent" declared in TOML and shipped with config push: it names the server functions and client tools the model may call, the events members record, its turn context and its limits, with model settings on a [configs.agent] configuration; while an agent uses a function, archiving or deleting it, or a schema change the agent cannot take, is refused with FUNCTION_USED_BY_AGENT.
  • A server function creates a session with ctx.agents.createSession, and members then use it through client.agents.sessions in the JavaScript and Swift clients: open returns a live view of the conversation — a synced database with the session's id, read from the device's copy — with onChange, send, answer, recordEvent, cancel, rename, addMember and removeMember act on it, and a member removed from the session sees the view empty, its gone set and the copy leave the device.
  • A tool can require a person's approval or be answered by the member's client, pausing the turn until the first valid answer, and ctx.tool.attachArtifact keeps an app-only value beside the call that the model never sees, which the app reads with the session view's artifact.
  • A turn's context — a server function's return or the send's own context, validated against the agent's schema — renders as turn.* in the system prompt, with the send's timezone and language as turn.timezone and turn.locale; an agent selects what the model sees of earlier turns with a history function or maxHistoryChars.
  • App owners and admins list, inspect and delete any member's sessions with primitive agent-sessions list, get and delete. primitive agent-sessions transcript, steps and artifacts read a session's messages, turn steps and tool-call artifacts by its session ID, for its members and console admins of the app (a tenant-side app owner or admin outside the session needs a grant on its document), and upload and download move its files; the system prompt and turn contexts stay visible only through get, to app owners and admins.
  • An open session view's attachments uploads a file to the session by its id alone, with no document ID in app code: upload() resolves once the file landed or, offline, once it is queued, queued uploads retry and survive a reload or restart in both clients, uploads(), pause(), resume(), cancel(), waitUntilUploaded() and read() manage and read them, and a send whose files name a queued upload waits for it (its pending entry shows the state waiting) and is sent once it lands. Once the session is deleted or the member removed, its queued uploads and the messages waiting on them fail with AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND. client.agents.sessions.uploadAttachment, downloadAttachment and attachmentHeaders do the same outside a view.
  • ctx.agents.createSession, getSession, listSessions, recordEvent and deleteSession take userId and work from any kind of run, cron, webhooks, nested starts, tools and context functions included: the session is owned, read, recorded or deleted as that member, else the invoking user, and only its owner deletes it. A tool, context or history function acts only for the turn's initiator. Only a REST client is refused AGENT_SESSION_ORIGIN_REFUSED.
  • A presentation tool (runs = "presentation") carries the structured data an agent hands the client with its final answer — result cards, follow-up chips: its call is final at once with the result { "delivered": true } and ends the turn with no further model round, and view.presentations() reads it in the JavaScript and Swift clients, typed by the agent's generated <Agent>AgentPresentation. A server tool declared with endsTurn = true ends the turn once it returns.
  • Every tool call of a turn carries callNumber, its number in the turn. A presentation's references name earlier results by that number, which the model reads with each result, and a number that names no earlier result of the turn is refused AGENT_PRESENTATION_REFERENCE_INVALID so the model corrects it.
  • Agent session list items and get() carry hasUnread and lastReadAt in both clients and in ctx.agents; client.agents.sessions.markRead(sessionId) (or view.markRead()) marks a session read for the user on every device, and primitive agent-sessions list shows an UNREAD column.
  • client.agents.sessions.watch() in the JavaScript and Swift clients keeps a session list current — the unread dot, last activity, title, status and members — without polling or opening any document, and refreshes it after a reconnect; an open view's info follows the same changes, and open(sessionId, { markRead: "while-open" }) keeps the open session read on the user's other devices. Each change is also the clients' agentSessionChanged event.
  • Agent session list items carry the session's status as of its last listed activity, in both clients and in ctx.agents.listSessions.
  • view.handleClientTools on an open agent session, in the JavaScript and Swift clients, runs a handler per client tool and answers each of the current user's waiting calls with the handler's result, including calls found again after a reconnect.
  • A turn's steps record each client tool call it waited on as a client_call step, timed from the call being written until its answer arrived, with resolvedByUserId naming the member who answered; a call that ends unanswered has its step failed with the code it ended with.

Child apps ​

  • primitive apps children create <slug> creates a child app of the current environment's app for a branch — a copy of its settings and, unless --no-secrets, its secrets — pushes the tree into it and selects it as a machine-local environment that config pull, push, diff, pnpm dev and the deploy scripts resolve with no other setup; apps children list, get and delete manage it, another parent admin attaches it with primitive env use <slug>, a child signs in with its parent environment's login so primitive login or logout in any of them acts on the whole tree, and primitive apps list --all includes children.
  • Every admin of the parent uses a child's admin and app APIs without an invitation; only the child's owner or the parent's console owner deletes it, and primitive apps delete <app-id> --with-children deletes an app's children before the app.
  • A child's own config var values go in primitive/<env>/vars.<slug>.override.toml beside vars.toml: with the child selected, config push sends vars.toml with the override's keys replacing or adding to it, config diff compares against those values, config pull writes the child's differing values into the override and never into vars.toml, and config set vars edits it; the parent and other children never read it. apps children create --vars-file <path> writes it before the first push, get shows it, delete removes it, and primitive init and the templates git-ignore primitive/*/*.override.toml. Functions cache the vars they read per version, so a child that adopts an override after its functions were pushed reads the new values once each function is pushed as a new version; config push notes when this applies.
  • A child is deleted after --idle-days (7–30, default 30) without a config push, an interactive sign-in or a person-started function invocation; its owner is emailed at least seven days before, and any such activity renews it.
  • pnpm cf-deploy --deploy-env <env> --primitive-env <child> --preview-alias <name> in the Vue template uploads a preview version of the worker under that alias with the child's app id, prints its URL and registers the origin on the child, so its CORS and email sign-in checks accept it while the live worker is untouched.
  • In the console, My Apps lists only apps with no parent, and an app's page lists its child apps and opens each one.
  • Apps made from the Vue and Swift templates give a line of work its own child app with pnpm child:up <slug> (scripts/child-app.sh up <slug> on iOS), which creates or resumes it, runs the app's scripts/child-app-init, pushes the tree and selects it; child:down runs scripts/child-app-teardown, deletes the child and selects the parent again.

Server functions ​

  • Breaking: A new or changed server function version must define an authorize method on the object form of defineFunction: authorize decides who may call it on every door — HTTP, agent, nested start, manual, webhook, cron and database change — with no owner or admin bypass, and a version without one is refused FUNCTION_AUTHORIZE_REQUIRED. An already-deployed version keeps its CEL access rule until you push a change; a version that carries both is refused FUNCTION_ACCESS_AMBIGUOUS, and the bare defineFunction(handler) form is deprecated.
  • Breaking: A version with authorize closes its inputSchema by default (additionalProperties: false), and config push refuses a function that admits anyone and can write unless its TOML says public = true (FUNCTION_PUBLIC_WRITE_UNDECLARED); it also refuses an inputSchema keyword the validator does not enforce (allOf, not, if, patternProperties, contains, a schema-valued additionalProperties, tuple items), naming the path.
  • Breaking: A function with authorize declares input: a call through HTTP, a nested start, --as system or an agent tool to a version with no input list is refused once authorize allows it, with 409 FUNCTION_INPUT_LIST_MISSING (an agent tool reads AGENT_TOOL_FAILED), and its handler does not run; this includes versions already deployed. config push refuses such a function with FUNCTION_INPUT_LIST_REQUIRED unless its TOML declares a trigger, and then warns; input: [] says the handler reads no input and needs no inputSchema. To migrate, add input: ["<key>", ...] or input: [] and push. A deployed version whose source already declares input but whose primitive functions get shows missing (caller calls refused) is repaired by config push from this CLI release; an older CLI skips the unchanged function, so upgrade the CLI or change the source.
  • An authorize version's handler receives only the input keys its input list names (defineFunction({ input: ["orderId"], authorize, handler })), and {} for input: [], on HTTP, nested, manual and tool calls; triggers and agent hooks still get the whole body, push refuses a listed key its inputSchema doesn't declare and warns about one authorize also resolves, primitive functions get shows the declared keys, and the handler's input type comes from the list.
  • A function that declares public = true answers callers who are not signed in once the app sets signedOutAccess = true in app.toml or the console's Settings: its authorize sees an anonymous auth.user, a version declaring public must have authorize (FUNCTION_PUBLIC_REQUIRES_AUTHORIZE), and a signed-out run that starts a task, calls an agent, sends a notification or changes a database the app does not hold is refused FUNCTION_SIGNED_OUT_REFUSED.
  • Signed-out calls, which a JavaScript or Swift client created without a token makes, are limited per IP address and by an hourly per-app ceiling that signedOutCeiling in app.toml sets, answering 429 with SIGNED_OUT_RATE_LIMITED or SIGNED_OUT_CEILING_REACHED, and primitive rate-counters get signed-out reads this hour's count.
  • Writing public = { cacheSeconds = 60, cors = "*" } in a function's TOML caches its signed-out answers for up to 300 seconds and accepts signed-out calls from any website, and primitive functions get prints the options.
  • primitive-functions exports allow, deny and fail, and the helpers allowAnyone, requireSignedIn, requireRole, requireMember, requireCollectionRole, requireDocument, requireCollection, requireRecord, hasGroupRole and allowCallers; authorize reads a read-only auth context, hands what it resolves to the handler as ctx.auth, and ctx.reauthorize() re-runs it mid-task against current data.
  • The generated declarations type each ctx.api call's body and answer from the platform's API spec, so config push's typecheck refuses a body key or an answer field the spec does not declare, and offer no field or call the platform does not serve.
  • A trigger fire or nested start that authorize refuses settles its run denied, a new terminal run status in both clients, the CLI and the console.
  • primitive functions authorize <key> runs only a function's authorize and prints the decision, with --user, --role, --trigger, --runtime and --input, and --cases runs the checks in functions/<key>.auth.json with @fixture aliases from auth-fixtures.json; the console shows each function's Authorize card and its denied invocations, and functions logs and functions get show the decision.
  • Breaking: config push refuses mode and durable in a function's TOML and mode on a [[function.triggers.cron]] entry, which it used to ignore with a warning: delete the lines — the caller picks the runtime with invoke or start — or let config pull strip them.
  • Breaking: The client doors to a one-request workflow run, a prompt and an integration are gone: in both clients workflows.runSync, client.prompts.execute and client.integrations.call are removed with their member routes, and generated workflow invokers drop runSync. Call a server function with functions.invoke and use ctx.prompts.run or ctx.integrations.call inside it.
  • Breaking: Registered database operations, database subscriptions and the clients' direct database surface are removed: config push refuses [[operations]] and [[subscriptions]] in a database type file, and the database operation and subscription commands and client methods are gone. Read and write records with ctx.db in a server function and publish changes with ctx.channels.publish.
  • Breaking: The workflow step DSL, Rhai scripts and standalone webhook and cron objects are retired: config push refuses workflow and script blocks, and primitive webhooks, primitive cron-triggers and the JavaScript client's cronTriggers are removed. Move the logic into a server function with webhook and cron triggers.
  • Server functions import code from directories outside the config tree, such as code your web client already runs, once functionSources in primitive/config.json lists them.
  • assertTrigger(ctx, kind) from primitive-functions refuses every trigger but kind and narrows ctx to it, so a tool function reads ctx.tool without a guard, and FunctionContextFor<kind> types a helper that takes the narrowed context.
  • ctx.users.forEachBatch and primitive users walk start run a batch function over every user a filter matches, under the users-batch trigger that allowCallers({ usersBatch }) admits, and primitive users walk status and terminate follow and stop a walk.
  • client.functions.listRuns lists the task runs the signed-in user started, filtered by function, status or document, and listRunSteps lists one run's steps, in both clients.
  • A document batch, ctx.api.documents.records.bulk and primitive documents records bulk accept an upsert operation that addresses a record by a declared unique constraint, compound or single-field: the record holding those values gets only the supplied fields, and a missing one is created. The result's new upserted list gives each upsert's record id and whether it was created.
  • A task run that shows no progress for 30 minutes is ended failed with the new errorCode FUNCTION_STALLED, so polling a run never needs a timeout of its own. A step's own timeout and retry delay extend the wait, and sleeps, event waits and retry delays never count.
  • A task run's slice block adds lastProgressAt, openStep, openStepStartedAt and parkedAt in both clients, and primitive functions runs shows a LAST PROGRESS column.
  • An integration call made inside a server function's step.do names its step in primitive integrations logs: a STEP column, --step <name> to filter, and correlation.stepId, correlation.stepOccurrence and detail.stepAttempt under --json.
  • Breaking: ctx.api.documents.blobs.uploadWithoutId is removed from primitive-functions; it only ever answered 405. Upload with ctx.api.documents.blobs.upload and a blobId you choose. The server no longer serves PUT /documents/{documentId}/blobs without an id.
  • A server function lists what a named member holds, page by page: ctx.api.documents.listOwnedByUser, ctx.api.documents.listSharedWithUser and ctx.api.collections.listForUser, each taking a userId. Over REST they are GET /users/{userId}/owned-documents, /shared-documents and /collections, for an app owner or admin.
  • A ctx.api call about one user names it in userId; omitted or empty, it means the invoking user. ctx.api.collections.list and the notifications inbox and device calls take it. In a run with no caller, a call that names nobody throws FUNCTION_SUBJECT_REQUIRED rather than answering empty or binding a user-scoped alias to no member, and documents.requestAccess throws it too.
  • Naming a user other than the invoking user is allowed in a run with no caller, one an app owner or admin invoked (the role read at each call), or one whose function declares the users:readAny capability (reads) or users:actAsAny (acting as the member). Any other run an ordinary member invoked, and every tool, context or history run and anything it starts, throws SUBJECT_USER_FORBIDDEN — on the calls above, the user-scoped alias calls, and collections.listForUser, documents.listOwnedByUser, documents.listSharedWithUser, groups.listUserMemberships and users.getRootDocument. A named user who is not a member throws SUBJECT_USER_NOT_FOUND.
  • Over REST, GET /collections, the notification routes and GET /agent-sessions/{sessionId} and /events take ?userId=: an app owner or admin names a member and gets that member's rows or view.
  • Breaking: A member naming another user on GET /agent-sessions?userId= or GET /users/{userId}/memberships is refused with code SUBJECT_USER_FORBIDDEN, replacing AGENT_SESSION_LIST_USER_FORBIDDEN and an uncoded Access denied.
  • ctx.api.invitations creates, reads, lists and deletes app invitations from a server function, at the member role and with the app's authority, so a function can invite an email that has no account without granting it anything.
  • Generated TypeScript and Swift types for function, prompt and agent schemas carry each constraint and annotation keyword — minLength, maximum, pattern, description, default and the rest — as a doc comment on the member or type it describes, so an editor hover shows the bounds the platform checks.
  • A function schema reuses a shape from its own $defs with "$ref" = "#/$defs/<Name>", or one declared in a schemas/ file by "$ref" = "schemas:<file>#/$defs/<Name>", ref = "schemas.<file>.<Name>" or the short ref = "<Name>" and ref = "<file>.<Name>", and push inlines the shape's definition and warns about a $ref it leaves unresolved; a schemas/ def uses another file's the same way, primitive schemas list and primitive schemas get read the pushed files, each pushed function version records which defs it inlined, and config diff names a function pinned to a def that has since changed, been removed or been deleted.
  • A function schema can be written as a field table in the db3 field grammar, under [function.input] and [function.output]: fields for an object, items, item.fields and open, the bounds min, max, min_length, max_length, pattern, min_items and max_items, nullable, coerce, ref and description, and schema = { ... } for anything else. Push compiles it to the JSON Schema it describes and stores the same schema the equivalent inputSchema stores, refuses a key the table does not take (such as a db3 storage key like indexed) naming the dotted path and the fix, and warns about a field-table key written under inputSchema.
  • A schemas/ def whose root carries a field-table key (fields, item, open, min, max, min_length, max_length, min_items, max_items, or a string items) is read as a field table, so a def that used one of those keys as an annotation gains the constraint on its next push, and push refuses a def that mixes them with properties, additionalProperties, a camelCase constraint such as minimum, $ref, $defs, oneOf, anyOf or const. Annotations such as title, format, readOnly and writeOnly beside them are kept; any other key in such a def is checked as a field table.
  • A function, prompt or agent schema uses a model of a db3 type by ref = "<type>.<model>", ref = "db3.<type>.<model>" or "$ref" = "db3:<type>#/$defs/<model>": an outputSchema gets the stored row (the declared fields, id and the type's timestamps and auto-populated fields) and every other schema the declared fields, #row or #declared chooses, validation messages and generated hovers name the projection, config push pushes a db3 type before the files that use it, and config diff names a schema pinned to a model that has since changed, been removed or been deleted.
  • pick = [...] or omit = [...] beside a db3 model ref, in a function, prompt or agent schema or a schemas/ def, keeps only some of the model's fields, each with the model's type: pick closes the object and omit keeps the projection's openness, functions codegen and the web and Swift clients type exactly those fields, a subset declared once as a schemas/ def is one named type, and push and codegen refuse a field the model does not have.
  • config diff previews the schemas a push changes: under each function, prompt and schemas/ file it lists each schema's changes classed additive, tightening or breaking, the refs the schema resolves (a db3 ref with its projection) and the generated types that change, and under a shared def, db3 type, function or prompt the objects pinned to it, including ones only the server holds; --json rows carry them as schemas and dependants.
  • A public function's public table takes rate = "low" | "medium" | "high", holding each signed-out IP address to 10, 60 or 300 calls of the function a minute (429 SIGNED_OUT_FUNCTION_RATE_LIMITED), and turnstile = true, which requires a body turnstileToken that Turnstile accepts on each signed-out call (403 SIGNED_OUT_TURNSTILE_REQUIRED or SIGNED_OUT_TURNSTILE_FAILED; 503 SIGNED_OUT_TURNSTILE_NOT_CONFIGURED or SIGNED_OUT_TURNSTILE_UNAVAILABLE). The app names its site key in [app] turnstileSiteKey, read signed out from GET settings/sign-in, and stores the secret as PRIMITIVE_TURNSTILE_SECRET. JavaScript client: functions.invoke(key, { turnstileToken }) sends the token and getAuthConfig() returns turnstileSiteKey. Pushing a turnstile function to an app with no site key or no secret succeeds with a warning naming what is missing: config push prints it, and the configs push answers it in warnings.
  • A server function holding the tokens:sign capability signs a link to another function of the app with ctx.actionTokens.sign({ functionKey, args, expiresIn, singleUse }), in beta, and that function's requireToken(tokenOf) admits whoever presents it, signed out included, with the bound arguments as ctx.auth.args; a refused link answers 404 NOT_FOUND with a message saying why, a single-use link is spent before the handler runs, push refuses cacheSeconds on a function that uses requireToken (FUNCTION_PUBLIC_CACHE_UNCACHEABLE_HELPER), and rotating JWT_SECRET voids every outstanding link.
  • requireInvitation(tokenOf) (beta) in a function's authorize admits whoever presents a token of an unaccepted, unexpired invitation of the app that still shares something, signed in or signed out, and resolves ctx.auth to { invitationId, inviterId, role, shared, sharedTruncated } with each shared item's id; any other token answers 404 NOT_FOUND. Its answers are never cached, and push refuses cacheSeconds on a version that uses it (400 FUNCTION_PUBLIC_CACHE_TOKEN_ADMITTED).
  • Breaking: PRIMITIVE_TURNSTILE_SECRET is reserved for Turnstile: a new function capability, CEL secrets entry, integration template, webhook trigger reference or Google clientSecret naming it is refused 400 RESERVED_SECRET_REFERENCE, while references saved before keep working; config push reports a function file whose capabilities newly name it before anything is applied. primitive secrets references <KEY> (GET …/secrets/by-key/{key}/references, beta) lists what in the app names a key, set or not, and secrets list and secrets set print each reference to the reserved key as a conflict.
  • Breaking: Pushing a server function or a schemas/ file needs primitive-admin 1.3.0 or newer: the server refuses a push from an older CLI with CLI_VERSION_TOO_OLD, and one without the compiled schemas a current CLI sends with COMPILED_PAYLOAD_REQUIRED, each naming the version to install. Run npm install -g primitive-admin@latest and push again.
  • Breaking: Generated types are one functions/primitive.d.ts, each schemas/ def, function, prompt, db3 model and user property type in its namespace (Schemas, Functions, Prompts, Db3, UserProperties): config push, config pull and primitive functions codegen remove primitive-function-types.d.ts, primitive-prompt-types.d.ts, primitive-db3-types.d.ts and primitive-user-properties.d.ts, printing a line for each, and push refuses a function source that still imports one; write import type { Functions, Schemas } from "./primitive" and Functions.<Key>Input; a top-level Primitive* name keeps its spelling.
  • Breaking: Generated types follow the compiled schemas: a field that refs a shared def or a db3 model is a reference to its one declaration (Schemas.Money, Db3.TasksRow) instead of unknown, and const, anyOf and nullable shape the type ("quote", A | B, T | null in TypeScript; a one-case enum, JSONValue and T? in Swift) instead of a doc comment.
  • Generated TypeScript invokers, agent client files and user property types export each enum's values as <Type><Field>Values = [...] as const, and functions codegen --lang swift writes Primitive.generated.swift, declaring each schemas/ def, prompt output type and referenced db3 row once for the per-key files to reference.
  • functions/primitive.d.ts declares a Db3.<Model>Filter and a Db3.<Model>Sort for each db3 model: annotate a ctx.db3 filter or sort with them, and config push's typecheck refuses an operator or a value that a declared field's kind doesn't take, such as $startsWith on a number. A field the model doesn't declare takes any operator. The ctx.db3 and auth.db3 model handles type the filters and sorts of query, count and aggregate the same way: a mismatch there is a config push warning in this release and the function still ships. Add a functions/ declaration file filling Db3FilterTyping to make it an error now.
  • Breaking: The production ctx.api and the primitive-functions types leave out the experimental methods, which production does not serve: ctx.api.resourceMetadata and the notifications inbox (notifications.list, unreadCount, markRead, markAllRead and send); the push-device methods stay. A function that calls them works only outside production; type it against primitive-functions@alpha, which keeps them.
  • A server function helper generic over a database type's model names reads, pages and writes through the typed ctx.db3 handle: primitive-functions exports Db3TypeModelName, Db3TypeRow, Db3TypeFilter, Db3TypeSort and Db3TypeBatchOp, each keyed by the type, and a filter or sort written inside such a helper is checked against every model the name may be, where it used to be refused under Db3FilterTyping.
  • primitive-functions/testing builds a FunctionContext and a FunctionStep for unit-testing a handler offline: createTestContext and createTestStep take overrides typed from the generated declarations, so an override that drifts from its member fails the typecheck; a member the test did not provide throws TEST_MEMBER_NOT_PROVIDED naming its path, step.do runs its body, and config push refuses a function whose bundle imports the module.
  • An invocation's log record carries timing, which splits durationMs into the phases the platform measured (waitMs, authorizeMs, startupMs, handlerMs, settleMs) and lists up to 50 of the function's ctx calls with how long each took; primitive functions logs --invocation and --run print a summary with the slowest calls.
  • Fixed: A webhook delivery signed with a newly created {{secrets.KEY}} signing secret verifies right away, instead of being refused with 401 for up to a minute.
  • Fixed: ctx.api.documents.blobs.upload stores the media type a server function names in "Content-Type", instead of always application/octet-stream.
  • Fixed: primitive functions codegen --lang swift leaves unchanged output files untouched, so an Xcode build no longer recompiles the whole app every time.
  • Fixed: Swift types generated from a function or agent schema now render three shapes the TypeScript types already did: an enum that repeats a value gets one case per value, where the generated Swift used to fail to compile, and an enum or a type list beside a oneOf that is not a valid tagged union renders as that enum or type, where --lang swift used to refuse the schema.
  • Fixed: invoke and start refuse an input that breaks a declared minLength, maxLength, maxItems, pattern or closed-object rule with 400 FUNCTION_INPUT_INVALID before the handler runs.
  • Fixed: A task run the platform could not begin settles failed with errorCode ENGINE_START_FAILED and no step run, instead of FUNCTION_THREW; the start retries for about a second before answering 500 INSTANCE_CREATE_FAILED.
  • Fixed: primitive functions codegen types a closed object schema with no properties key as the empty object it is, the same as properties = {}: an empty struct in Swift and {} in TypeScript.
  • Fixed: Concurrent config pushes of the same new function with a cron trigger no longer answer 500; each succeeds and the function gets one cron schedule.
  • Fixed: A task run whose runtime storage fails mid-run is kept open for the runtime to resume, instead of every later step, the run's failure handling included, failing at once without running.

Large documents ​

  • Breaking: Large documents are record-log documents (documentFormat: 3) and the earlier large-document format is no longer served: creating or opening a documentFormat: 2 document fails with DOCUMENT_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, and --large creates the new format; load an earlier export into a new large document with primitive documents ingest.
  • A large document is created with documentFormat: 3 (CLI: primitive documents create --format 3, or --large) and opens through the same document, model and query APIs in the JavaScript and Swift clients, and a write the platform cannot keep comes back on the document:write-refused event with every withdrawn write.
  • An app bulk loads records into a large document from its own code with documents.ingests in the JavaScript and Swift clients, and primitive documents ingests lists, inspects and aborts a document's load sessions.
  • A large document's snapshot reuses the chunks that did not change, so a client that holds an earlier one downloads only the rest.
  • primitive documents inspect reports a large document's write progress, writers and bulk load, and --refused lists the rows a load refused; primitive documents ingest takes --mode refresh to delete the records a load does not name.
  • In Node.js, a large document stays on disk across restarts with databaseConfig: { type: "node-sqlite", options: { recordLogDirectory } }, and a document's GET /documents/{documentId}/schema adds an observed section with the kinds each undeclared field has held.
  • A large document's fields hold a string, a number, a boolean, null or an array of strings, on every write path: an array of strings is a string set wherever it is written (membership queries find it; an array replaces its members, { $add, $remove, $clear } from record routes and server functions change them, null empties it), a field keeps the string-set or scalar kind of its first non-null value, a model takes at most 1,000 field names, and field and model names are identifiers. A write outside these rules — an object, an array of anything but strings, the other kind, the 1,001st field name — is refused with DOCUMENT_ENTRY_INVALID, naming the model and field, and a bulk load's refused row carries the reason, which documents inspect --refused prints.

Documents ​

  • Breaking: documents.validateAccess on a document the server does not hold — deleted, never existed, or in another app — answers 404 NOT_FOUND in both clients instead of DOCUMENT_DELETED; on a document whose create has not yet reached the server it waits for the commit and answers owner, failing with PENDING_CREATE when the device is offline or the create has not landed within 30 seconds.
  • Breaking: In the functions SDK, ctx.api.documents.blobs.downloadUrl is now download: it returns the blob's bytes, as before. Rename the calls in your functions. The JavaScript and Swift clients' downloadUrl, which returns a URL, is unchanged.
  • A document record query, ctx.doc(id).model(name).query in a server function or primitive documents records query, takes a sort (--sort) and answers 100 records by default and up to 10,000 on request, refusing a larger limit with 400 instead of clamping it.
  • An app admin, in-app or console, can delete any document of the app directly with documents.delete, as an app owner already could.
  • Fixed: A compound unique constraint holds across writers: a record saved by a server function, a workflow, the REST API or the CLI now blocks a client save of the same values, and the reverse.
  • Fixed: me.sharedDocuments() no longer skips documents when paging with a small limit. A page can now be short or empty while hasMore is true; keep following nextCursor.
  • Fixed: The dev tools' Document and Blob explorers and the Swift PrimitiveAppState.fetchDocuments() list every owned and shared document, not only the first page of each, and fetchDocuments() lists the locally cached documents while the server's page is pending, replacing them when it arrives.
  • Fixed: A document listing fetched for a user who has since signed out is dropped instead of being kept for the next signed-in user, in both clients.
  • Fixed: A save from a server function, the REST API or the CLI no longer duplicates a unique value held by a record the constraint's index has no entry for (one written before the constraint existed, or imported); the save is refused with the unique-constraint error, so a connected JavaScript client no longer drops the original record.
  • Fixed: In the Swift client, an openDocument that waits on the network always resolves or throws .networkTimeout within availabilityWait, and setLogLevel(.debug) traces each open.
  • Fixed: In the Swift client, documents cached on a device for one user, pending creates included, no longer load for another user who signs in on the same device.
  • Fixed: In the Swift client, logout(wipeLocal: true) deletes only the signed-out user's local documents, instead of every user's on the device, another user's unsynced creates included.
  • Fixed: Two documents that each hold a record with the same id keep their own records in the client's local query tables, so a count() or query() scoped to one of them no longer comes back short; a local store written by an earlier release is rebuilt on its next open and keeps every row.

Models and queries ​

  • Breaking: A stringset field's values are returned sorted by Unicode code point, each value once, from every surface — model reads, queries, server reads, the CLI and the Swift client, in documents, large documents and databases — rather than in the order they were added; sort a copy to display another order.
  • Breaking: aggregate answers an array of rows instead of an object keyed by group value: one row per group, { group: { <field>: <value> }, count, <type>_<field> }, on the model statics in both clients, document and database aggregates, server functions, the Swift DoDb.aggregate and the CLI. Every operation keeps its key even when it is the only one, group values keep their type, an ungrouped server aggregate is one row with an empty group, and two groupBy entries that would share a key throw Ambiguous aggregation group keys.
  • Breaking: In a server function, ctx.doc(id).model(name).aggregate resolves to the rows themselves; HTTP, the CLI's --json and ctx.db(...).model(...).aggregate keep the { result } envelope around them.
  • Breaking: A model field cannot take a name a generated model already uses on either client, such as syncState, save or related (the models guide lists them): codegen refuses a schema that declares one, and a record write carrying one fails with RESERVED_FIELD_NAME.
  • Breaking: createModelClass is removed from js-bao and the JavaScript client: define a model as a class that extends BaseModel and attach its schema with defineModelSchema and attachAndRegisterModel.
  • aggregate groups a date field by calendar month, quarter or year with a { field, period } groupBy entry, keyed <field>_<period> in each row's group, on the model statics in both clients and on a document's model in a server function.
  • The JavaScript client's registerModelTimeoutMs option sets how long client.registerModel waits for databases still connecting before it rejects REGISTER_MODEL_TIMEOUT.
  • Fixed: A query whose projection names a stringset field returns the field's values instead of an empty set.
  • Fixed: A membership groupBy ({ field, contains }) on the JavaScript model statics answers one complete row per value, where it used to answer a group per record when more than one record carried the member.

Collections ​

  • Breaking: Collections have fixed roles — owner, manager, editor, contributor and viewer — held by users and groups as principals: collection type configs are gone (config push refuses a collection-type-configs/ file), and collectionType, permission on members, getAccess, grantGroupPermission and revokeGroupPermission are deprecated in both clients in favour of role, listMembers, addGroupMember, setMemberRole and removeMember; existing collections were migrated to roles.
  • A collection has a custodian who holds owner and cannot leave until it is transferred: a server function or the admin API names one with custodian (app, or a member) on collections.create, and collections.transfer, primitive collections transfer, collections list --custodian, resolveRole and settings.memberList in both clients, the CLI and server functions, and requireCollectionRole in a function's authorize, work with it. Collections and groups a removed member held pass to the app when anyone else holds a role on them and are deleted otherwise, and a transfer in progress answers 409 TRANSFER_PENDING.
  • Breaking: Collection contextId is removed from the API, rules, both clients and the CLI; bind a collection to an outside entity with initialMetadata on create and read it in rules as md.self.<category>.<key>.
  • Breaking: Collection names are labels, not unique within an app, so creating or renaming a collection never answers a name 409, and primitive collections import refuses a name that more than one target collection carries.
  • Fixed: A collection's documentCount stays accurate when documents are added to or removed from it at the same time.
  • Fixed: Deleting or unsharing a collection shared with a group, removing a document from it, and revoking a document's group grant no longer fail with 403 on older grants.

Users and groups ​

  • Breaking: Groups have fixed roles — owner, manager and member — and are addressed by groupId alone: group type configs and their rule sets are gone (config push refuses a group-type-configs/ file), the (groupType, groupId) forms of the group methods in both clients, groupType on create and grants, and isMemberOf(groupType, groupId) / memberGroups(groupType) in rules are deprecated in favour of the one-argument forms, and existing groups were migrated to roles with their creators as owners.
  • Breaking: A client session can no longer create a group (403 FUNCTION_ROUTE_FUNCTION_ONLY): create one from a server function with ctx.api.groups.create or from the admin API (primitive groups create --owner <user-id>, or the console), naming a custodian and initial members; the server assigns every group's id and refuses a create that names one.
  • primitive groups members add takes an existing app user's email, and primitive waitlist bulk-invite --ids invites the entries you name.
  • Every group has a custodian — the member holding the owner row, or the app — and settings.memberList; addMember takes a role, setMemberRole changes it, groups.transfer (primitive groups transfer) hands the group to another member, a function lists a custodian's groups with listByCustodian and gates on a role with hasGroupRole(groupId, role), and granting a group a database permission or a collection role needs a membership in that group or the app owner or admin role (GROUP_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED).
  • The console's Groups pages work by id, with a Custodian column, member roles, an owner-row control and a transfer dialog, and Manage User shows a member's holdings.
  • groups.create accepts initialMetadata from ctx.api.groups.create and primitive groups create --initial-metadata.
  • An app owner or admin sets a user's display name and avatar, at creation or later: primitive users create --name --avatar-url, primitive users set-profile <user-id> --name|--avatar-url|--clear-avatar, ctx.api.users.setProfile from a server function, and name/avatarUrl when adding a user by email. An avatar URL written this way or by me.update must be an http: or https: URL; any other scheme is refused with 400 and nothing is written.
  • User listings mark each +primitivetest test user with testUser, and primitive users list --test-users exclude|only, testUsers on GET /users and ctx.api.users.list, and the console's Users page filter them out or show only them.
  • ctx.users.query, count and aggregate in a server function, the admin API and primitive users query, count and aggregate search an app's users by their base fields and declared properties (properties.<name>), and primitive users index shows the user index's status, rebuilds it and reconciles it.
  • user-properties.toml declares an app's typed user properties: config push publishes the schema, primitive user-properties get shows the active one, and codegen types them as UserProperties in server functions and both clients.
  • A server function reads and writes user properties with ctx.users.get, setProperties, addToSet and removeFromSet, and finds the user holding a unique value with ctx.users.getBy or primitive users get-by.
  • A property's client setting lets signed-in clients read it on me.get and the user lookups, and lets users write their own with me.update({ properties }), in both clients.
  • initialProperties on an invitation, primitive users invite --initial-properties or primitive users create --initial-properties gives a new user their properties at signup, and ctx.invitations.getBy finds a pending invitation by a unique value.
  • primitive metadata report user reports which user metadata categories still hold rows on an app's current members, with their counts.
  • GET invitations/preview?inviteToken= (beta) shows what an invitation offers before its holder signs in, with no session and in every app: the app's name and icon, the inviter's name, the offered role, the databases, groups and collections it shares, the masked email and its status. The JavaScript client's invitations.preview(inviteToken) and primitive users invitations preview <inviteToken> call it. An unknown or revoked token answers 404 INVITATION_NOT_FOUND, which counts toward the per-address limit on failed accepts.
  • revokePendingInvitation on groups and collections, in both clients and ctx.api, cancels one email share before the invitee signs up, keyed by the invitationId from listPendingInvitations, and leaves the invitation's other grants in place.
  • Deprecated: invitations.listDeferredGrants and revokeDeferredGrant in both clients, and the deferred-grants routes they call; list and revoke a pending invitation on its database, group or collection.
  • Deprecated: Resource metadata — client.resourceMetadata in both clients, ctx.api.resourceMetadata, primitive metadata get, set, list, delete, get-batch and resolve, and the routes they call — stays served; keep per-user data in user properties, and group or collection data in a db3 database keyed by the group or collection id. primitive metadata report is not deprecated.
  • Fixed: An invitation for an email that already belongs to a member, or already has a pending invitation, is refused with 400 USER_ALREADY_MEMBER or INVITATION_PENDING in any letter case, instead of creating a second invitation.
  • Fixed: The admin API's app users list (GET /admin/api/apps/{appId}/users) returns every member of an app, instead of at most the first 100.

Usage ​

  • Primitive meters what each app uses (requests, function runs and steps, AI tokens, realtime messages, emails, rows read and written, and stored bytes), and primitive usage and the admin API's usage routes read it by meter, day, user and origin with an estimated cost.
  • A server function reads one member's usage with ctx.usage.forUser, and in the JavaScript client a member reads their own, or an app owner or admin any member's, with client.usage.forUser.
  • An app admin reads the counter behind a rate limit by its key with primitive rate-counters get, in beta.
  • primitive usage get --meter <meter> prints one meter's quantity for each day of the month, such as signedout.invoke and signedout.ceiling_refused for the signed-out calls the hourly ceiling accepted and refused.

Analytics ​

  • primitive analytics filters events with a repeatable --where <field><op><value>, takes --fresh to bypass the short-lived answer cache, and reads activity with no signed-in user with user-detail --anonymous.
  • Analytics leaves +primitivetest test users out of active-user counts, cohort retention and top users by default, keeps them in the event feed, and lets --test-users exclude|include|only on primitive analytics, testUsers on the REST queries and ctx.api.analytics, and the console's Test users control choose.
  • Fixed: A burst of tracked events is stored whole instead of losing every event past the first 250, and events that still cannot be stored are counted in an analytics_relay error group (primitive analytics errors-groups --source analytics_relay).

Locks ​

  • Breaking: Locks belong to server functions only: client.locks and its types are removed from the JavaScript and Swift clients, the lock rule set is retired (config push refuses it), and the acquire, renew and release routes refuse any caller but a function with 403 FUNCTION_ROUTE_FUNCTION_ONLY.
  • A server function waits for a named lock with ctx.locks.acquire, or runs code under it with ctx.locks.withLock, and an app admin inspects and frees the app's locks with primitive locks list, status and force-release.

Prompts ​

  • Deprecated: accessRule on a prompt or an integration is ignored and will be removed in the first breaking release after 2026-12-15: the calling function's authorize (and, for an integration, its integration:<key> capability) decides who may run it; config push warns once per file that still carries it, and config pull rewrites the file without it.
  • Breaking: config push refuses a prompt schema keyword a Gemini configuration cannot carry without loss, such as exclusiveMinimum or uniqueItems, or a free-form object (PROMPT_SCHEMA_NOT_TRANSLATABLE), and one the platform does not enforce, such as allOf (PROMPT_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORD), naming the path and the fix, before it sends anything, and config diff reports the file as invalid; the admin API's prompt and configuration writes refuse it with 400 and every refusal under details.refusals, as do a switch to Gemini, a restore and a duplicate that would send such a schema to Gemini.
  • Breaking: A Gemini prompt run sends its outputSchema to the model with its meaning kept — unions, nullable types and constants included — and a stored schema with a keyword Gemini cannot carry fails before any model request with errorCode PROMPT_SCHEMA_NOT_TRANSLATABLE, from ctx.prompts.run, primitive prompts execute, prompt tests and evaluators.
  • Breaking: ctx.prompts.run validates a prompt's answer against every keyword of its outputSchema, so a value outside minLength, pattern, maximum or another constraint fails with PROMPT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION.
  • A prompt's inputSchema and outputSchema, a configuration's outputSchema and an agent's tool, event and turn-context schemas use shapes from their own $defs, schemas/ files, other prompts' schemas (ref = "prompt.<key>.output", prompt.<key>.tools.<name>.input, prompt.<key>.events.<kind>) and functions' (fn.<key>.input), and push inlines them, pushing each prompt after what it refs; config push --only prompt/<key> also pushes the prompts and schemas/ files the selection refs, config pull writes the refs back, a prompt written from the console or the admin API is compiled the same way, and config diff names a prompt pinned to a shape that has since changed or been deleted.
  • A prompt's schemas can be written as field tables too: [prompt.input], [prompt.output] and [configs.chat.output], an agent tool's input and output, and the field-table keys directly on an agent event or the turn context, in place of schema. config pull writes a prompt's schemas back as JSON Schema.
  • A prompt names the prompt that judges its test cases by default with defaultEvaluatorPromptKey in [prompt], primitive prompts execute --attach <path> sends files with a run, and primitive prompts and primitive integrations tests runs list page with --cursor while tests runs get reads one run.
  • primitive integrations test sends headers, url-encoded forms, multipart fields and files, or a raw body (--header, --form, --field, --file, --raw-body, --content-type).
  • A test case on an agent prompt runs one model round from a conversation it writes in a [test.agent] block — user and assistant messages, tool calls with their results, and events — with the round's turn context, timezone and locale. expectedToolCall and expectedNoToolCall check the calls the model made, the text checks and an evaluator work as for a chat prompt, and every run records a Round completed check with the calls. A case that cannot be a round of its agent is refused with AGENT_TEST_CASE_INVALID.
  • A prompt run whose answer stopped at the configuration's maxTokens carries truncated: true, on success and on failure, from ctx.prompts.run and primitive prompts execute. A cut-off JSON answer, or a completion that used the whole limit and returned nothing, fails with the new errorCode PROMPT_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED instead of PROMPT_OUTPUT_NOT_JSON or PROMPT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION; raise maxTokens. primitive prompts execute prints a warning, and a prompt test run cut off at the limit fails its Output complete check.
  • Breaking: config push refuses a prompt [[configs]] entry that writes chat keys at its root or marks the live config with isActive, so move those keys under [configs.chat] and write active = true.
  • Fixed: OpenRouter chat configurations now send maxTokens to the provider, so a configuration that sets it is capped at that many output tokens.
  • Fixed: config push no longer refuses a reasoning setting because of which values a particular model supports; the provider decides. A value the model refuses fails the run with the provider's message, upstreamStatus: 400 and the new errorCode PROMPT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED, from ctx.prompts.run and primitive prompts execute. A provider 400 on any prompt run carries that code.
  • Fixed: A prompt run with strictOutput = true and a modelOverride that does not support strict structured outputs fails before any model request, as config push already refuses for the configured model.
  • Fixed: primitive prompts execute, the console's prompt test and the evaluator use a system prompt or user template larger than 25 KB (stored offloaded) instead of running without it.
  • Fixed: ctx.prompts.run's metrics is typed PromptRunMetrics in the functions SDK, so a function reads inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, reasoningTokens, cost and durationMs without a cast.

Sign-in and sessions ​

  • Breaking: magicLinkRequest, otpRequest and their routes are removed, and the auth and app config report only emailSignInEnabled; start email sign-in with emailSignInRequest.
  • An emailed sign-in link opens the page that asked for it: emailSignInRequest links to the page's origin by default, redirectUri: null asks for a code only, and handleSignInCallback on the JavaScript client and auth.handleSignInCallback on the Swift client finish a sign-in from its callback URL, emailed link and OAuth redirect alike.
  • Breaking: emailSignInRequest with no redirectUri and no oauthRedirectUri set links to the page's origin plus /oauth/callback by default, where it used to send a code-only email: add that URL to the app's [auth].emailRedirectUris and run config push, or pass redirectUri: null to keep asking for a code only. A call that already passes a redirectUri, or a client with oauthRedirectUri set, is unaffected.
  • A Node script, cron job or CI step signs the JavaScript client in as a user with no browser or password by passing an app access token from primitive tokens create as token.
  • GET /app/{appId}/api/settings/sign-in reads an app's public sign-in settings with no session, and getAuthConfig(), getAppConfig(), checkOAuthAvailable() and Google sign-in in both clients read them there.
  • [app] iconUrl (an https: URL) and brandColor (# and six hex digits) brand an app's pages: PUT settings and config push set them (400 INVALID_ICON_URL or INVALID_BRAND_COLOR on a bad value), and GET settings/sign-in and getAuthConfig() return them.
  • A browser passkey request from a host with no relying party of its own runs under the longest configured relying party that host is a subdomain of.
  • Deprecated: GET /app/{appId}/api/oauth-config; read settings/sign-in, which answers the same body.
  • Fixed: Clearing an app's googleClients or passkeyRpConfig from the console no longer brings back Google client or passkey values set before those maps existed.
  • Fixed: The plain-text part of an email, the sign-in link included, carries its links as written instead of HTML-escaped (&amp;), in built-in templates, template overrides and ctx.api.email.send.

API and clients ​

  • Breaking: The JavaScript client's appVersion option must be a dotted version such as "2.4.0", and platform a lowercase name; any other value now throws INVALID_ARGUMENT when the client is built.
  • Breaking: The JavaScript client loads Yjs and y-indexeddb the first time it opens a document with Yjs state, so an app that only uses databases never loads them: keep yjs installed as a peer dependency, import "yjs"; once to keep it in the startup bundle, and in a browser await loadYjs() from js-bao before calling js-bao's Y.Doc helpers, which throw YjsNotLoadedError until Yjs is loaded.
  • Breaking: The database CEL context, deprecated in the last release, is removed: getCelContext/updateCelContext and the database metadata methods in both clients, primitive databases cel-context and databases create --cel-context/--metadata, the databases/{databaseId}/metadata routes, and celContext/metadata on database responses. A rule that still references database.celContext or $database.metadata is refused when saved.
  • Breaking: List responses drop the deprecated cursor alias and the grants, admins, apps, documents and databases array keys, so read rows from items and page with nextCursor; the Swift client's DeferredGrantListResult drops its grants property and init(grants:) initializer the same way — read items and build pages with init(items:nextCursor:hasMore:).
  • Breaking: The deprecated admin-data/* database record routes and ctx.api.databases.adminData in primitive-functions are removed; use the records/* routes and ctx.api.databases.records.
  • Breaking: The deprecated primitive databases permissions grant and revoke commands and the JavaScript client's databases.grantPermission and revokePermission are removed; use primitive databases permissions add-manager / remove-manager, or ctx.api.databases.addManager / revokePermission from a server function.
  • Breaking: The JavaScript client removes FunctionWaitForResult, documents.createOffline, waitForSync and updateLocalSnapshotFlag (use FunctionRunSettled, documents.create and waitForInitialSync), and both clients drop user_created_at_epoch_s from analytics event input.
  • Breaking: In the Swift client, an HTTP call made while the client is offline throws JsBaoError with code .offline without sending the request, as the JavaScript client does, so code that detects a missing network by catching JsBaoNetworkError must also catch .offline.
  • Breaking: A retention policy's maxDocs and TTL (ttlMs, Swift ttl) must be positive in both clients: 0, which the JavaScript client read as no limit and the Swift client as evict everything, is refused INVALID_ARGUMENT, so omit the field (Swift nil) for no limit.
  • Breaking: On production, experimental surfaces are not served — the notification inbox and sending, the notification event, resource metadata and its categories, and rule-set debug answer 404 to the clients and are refused to server functions, while every other environment serves them.
  • Breaking: The production builds of the JavaScript and Swift clients leave out the experimental members client.notifications, client.resourceMetadata and ruleSets.debug, which production does not serve; their payload types and the notification event stay. An app that uses them works only outside production; build it against js-bao-wss-client@alpha or the Swift package's alpha branch, which keep them.
  • Both clients report connected once the server can deliver the user's events to them — notifications, document metadata, agent sessions and access requests — so a list made on connect and the events that follow miss nothing; a connection that never gets there within the sync handshake timeout is retried.
  • In a browser tab, the JavaScript client keeps its connection id across reloads, and each tab has its own, so a reload reconnects about a second sooner and a connection id your app stored still reaches the same tab.
  • Every public method of the JavaScript and Swift clients states its stability — production, beta or experimental — in its doc comment, and deprecated ones are struck through in editors or warn at compile time with their successor.
  • A request to a known path with a method it does not accept answers 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED with an Allow header, on the app and admin APIs.
  • Deprecated: In the JavaScript client, client.ruleSets (author rule sets in rule-sets/ and config push), notifications.send (send from a server function) and getBlobManager() (use client.db3.blobs(db3Id)), and in both clients collections.listAll.
  • Fixed: A database record saved without an id is given one, as documented, instead of being refused.
  • Fixed: A WebSocket connection opened with an access token is closed when the token is revoked, deleted or expires, instead of staying open.
  • Fixed: The JavaScript client bypasses the browser's HTTP cache on every request, so concurrent reads of the same resource no longer wait on one another.
  • Fixed: A WebSocket connection opened with an access token, or reopened right after a disconnect, is no longer closed with 4001 SESSION_INVALID the next time it sends after a quiet period.
  • Fixed: In the JavaScript client, going back online soon after goOffline keeps the new connection, instead of dropping it and resetting every open document when the old connection's close arrives late.
  • Fixed: In the Swift client, queued blob uploads survive a process restart and are sent by the next client for the same app and user, as the JavaScript client's do; an upload queued by one user is never attempted, listed or cancelled while another user is signed in.
  • Fixed: In Node.js, a better-sqlite3 that is installed but not built fails sign-in with STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE naming the fix, instead of signing in without a session store; a client that is not installed still falls back to the in-memory store, and storageConfig: { type: "memory" } chooses it outright.
  • Fixed: A browser build of an app using the JavaScript client no longer bundles better-sqlite3 or warns about externalized Node built-ins or a missing y-indexeddb default export, and the Vue template's build prints none of those warnings.

App hosting ​

  • primitive hosting deploy <dir> --slug <slug> publishes a static web front end at https://<slug>.primitive.app, uploading only changed files and waiting until the origin serves them, with spa or static routing, and primitive hosting get, deployments, activate, disable, enable and rename manage it.
  • The deploy that claims a slug, and every rename, adds the hosted origin to the app's CORS origins, email redirect URIs, passkey relying parties and Google client redirect URIs and pushes them; primitive hosting trust repeats the step, and --no-trust prints the entries instead.
  • A hosted build, such as the Vue template's pnpm build:hosted, reads its app id, API and WebSocket URLs and sign-in proxy from /__primitive/config.json, so one build runs as whichever app it is deployed to, and auth.refreshProxy.passkey: true in the JavaScript client sends passkey sign-in and registration through that proxy too.

Configuration and CLI ​

  • Client versions.
